$comment: REVIEWED AND PINNED. This catalog is acted upon: a class below can create a
real sandbox that runs repository code.
Administrator-controlled sandbox class catalog for Squad on ACA.
This file is owned by the Squad on ACA control plane (this repository), NOT
by the repositories Squad works on. A worked-on repository's
squad-capabilities.yml can only *request* capabilities; it can never add a
class, add an egress destination, widen a credential list, name a shell
command, or select an arbitrary image. image.hint from a manifest is matched
against imageHintAliases below purely to disambiguate between already-approved
classes; it is NEVER executed or used as an image reference.
"provisional": false means an administrator has reviewed image.digest,
resources, limits, egress.hostRules, allowedCredentials and approved for every
class. Every APPROVED class must carry image.pinned: true and a real
image.digest: a sandbox is created from an immutable digest, never from a
moving tag, so re-tagging a repository cannot change what runs. image.tag is
recorded for humans only and is not used to launch anything.
BOTH APPROVED CLASSES CURRENTLY PIN THE SAME IMAGE: the squad-worker image
built from this repository's worker/Dockerfile. There is no separate
per-language image yet, so a class's `tools` list is the CONTRACT the class
offers to routing, not an inventory read out of the image. The enforcing gate
is worker/lib/squad-capability-preflight.sh, which runs INSIDE the sandbox
before any repository code and fails closed if a declared tool is absent. A
class that over-claims therefore costs a refused session, never an unsafe one.
What actually differentiates these classes from the default worker today is
allowedCredentials and egress, both of which are enforced by the control plane
before the sandbox starts.
egress mirrors the real Azure Container Apps Sandboxes network policy shape
(Microsoft.App/sandboxGroups, api-version 2026-02-01-preview): a defaultAction,
an ordered hostRules[] of {pattern, action}, and trafficInspection. Patterns are
either an exact host or a leading-wildcard suffix ("*.github.com" matches any
host ending in ".github.com", and does not match the bare apex). Rules are
evaluated in order; the first match wins; defaultAction applies when none match.
Squad workers must run in an identity-free sandbox group (managed identity on
ACA Sandboxes is group-scoped, so an identity on the group would be reachable
from inside the sandbox).
TWO ENTRIES BELOW ARE ENFORCED, NOT ADVISORY (PRD #6, Sprint 7/8):
- limits.maxConcurrentSandboxes bounds live sandboxes per class. A class with
no such limit is a CONFIGURATION ERROR and refuses to dispatch; it is never
read as 'unbounded'.
- egress.defaultAction must be "Deny". A repository's manifest may only
NARROW hostRules; a requested destination the template does not already
permit is a hard failure, and no emitted rule may lack template provenance.
trafficInspection "Full" means TLS INTERCEPTION: enforcing an allowlist on
hostnames and paths requires terminating TLS, so the inspecting proxy is inside
the trust boundary and sees plaintext request bodies. That is a deliberate
trade (see docs/runbook.md, incident runbook R3) and must be understood before
a third party's data is put through a sandbox.

defaultWorker.description: The fixed squad-worker image running as an ACA job. This is the current, unchanged execution path.

classes.description: Node/JavaScript toolchain with private-registry auth. Pinned to the squad-worker image by digest. Its distinguishing capability over the default worker is NODE_AUTH_TOKEN/NPM_TOKEN plus a default-deny egress policy.
Python 3.12 toolchain. Pinned to the squad-worker image by digest. Its distinguishing capability over the default worker is a default-deny egress policy that permits the Python package indexes.

Container build tooling. NOT APPROVED and NOT PINNED: a usable Docker daemon inside a sandbox needs its own security review, and no image has been built for it, so this class must never be selected. Present so the catalog documents the gap and the resolver's approved-only filter is exercised. Approving it requires building an image and pinning its digest here first.
